title: Nash-Williams fronts and 2-better-quasi-orders
abstract: Formalizes Nash-Williams fronts through their well-founded prefix trees and ordinal ranks, proves the finite-color Nash-Williams theorem, and derives the infinite Ramsey theorem for arbitrary finite arity. The order-theoretic development proves that 2-better-quasi-orders are well-quasi-orders and establishes closure under finite products, lexicographic sums, domination of subsets, and pointwise embedding of sequences. Throughout, TwoBQO r is the good-triple property of an arbitrary binary relation r (every pair-sequence has m < n < l with f(m,n) related to f(n,l)); it assumes no reflexivity or transitivity of r.

informal.Front.IsFront.nash_williams: Every two-coloring of a Nash-Williams front on an infinite set has an infinite restriction whose front is monochromatic.
informal.Front.IsFront.nash_williams_fin: Every finite coloring of a Nash-Williams front has an infinite restriction whose front is monochromatic.
informal.infinite_ramsey: Every finite coloring of the r-element subsets of an infinite set of natural numbers is constant on all r-element subsets of some infinite subset.
informal.TwoBQO.lexSigmaQO: The 2-BQO good-triple property is preserved by lexicographic sums: if the index relation and every fibre relation have it, so does the lexicographic-sum relation on the sigma type. This asserts nothing about reflexivity or transitivity of the sum; those are proved separately (LexSumRelQO.refl and LexSumRelQO.trans) under the corresponding order hypotheses on the index and fibres.
informal.TwoBQO.embedForAll_wqo: If a preorder is a 2-better-quasi-order, then its infinite sequences are well-quasi-ordered by the relation admitting a strictly monotone reindexing along which corresponding terms are related.
